This appeal is filed by the insurer calling in question the judgment and award passed on 05.04.2023 in MVC No.426/2020, by Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge and JMFC, Bidar and MACT, Bidar on ground of liability and quantum

. 
2. Heard Sri Sudharshan M., learned counsel for appellant and Sri Basavaraj R Math, learned counsel for respondents No.1 to 6.
3.
Sri Sudharshan M., learned counsel taking this Court through the judgment and award passed by tribunal would contend that owner of the vehicle remained ex-parte.
Police have registered case against the driver of the offending vehicle invoking provisions of Section 181 of M.V. Act and Section 184 of M.V. Act against the owner of the offending vehicle.
Owner of offending vehicle remained ex-parte and not challenged the provisions stated supra.

The insurance company examined its officials to prove their case that the owner NC: 2025:KHC-K:4513-DB HC-KAR engaged the driver,
who did not have a valid driving license.

However, Tribunal has not considered said aspect of the matter and fastened liability on the insurance company to pay compensation at first instance and recover the same later, from the owner of offending vehicle.

To buttress his arguments he lied on judgment of Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.6154/2019 dated 14.12.2023 and MFA No.3297/2019 dated 13.04.2023 contending that, if the case is made out that the owner of the offending vehicle permitted the person not having valid driving license to drive, then insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

It is the owner of the offending vehicle, i.e. insured,
who is liable to pay compensation.

Insofar as, Tribunal having considered the married daughters as dependants of deceased, he submits that daughters were married and had gone out of family and hence, they are not entitled to be considered as dependents on the deceased.

To buttress his arguments, he relied on judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Deep Shikha and Anr. V.
National Insurance Company Ltd. And Ors., in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
Nos.22265-22266/2018 decided on 13.06.2025, particularly on paragraphs No.13 and 14, where it is held that NC: 2025:KHC-K:4513-DB HC-KAR married daughters are not entitled to be considered Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. 4 as dependants on the deceased while considering deduction towards personal expenses.

sentences.text: On these grounds, he sought to allow the appeal and set aside the judgment and order passed by Tribunal fastening liability on the insurance company to pay compensation at first instance and recover same from the insured.

4. Refuting the submission of learned counsel for appellant, Sri Basavaraj R Math, contended that the facts of the case in the judgments relied upon by counsel for appellants and facts of case on hand are entirely different.

In case of judgment of Division Bench of this Court, there is clear finding that the insurer consciously or knowingly well of the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving license, engaged him to drive the vehicle.
Those are the circumstances, under which Division Bench passed an order that the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.

Insofar as contention about married daughters is concerned, the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of National Insurance NC: 2025:KHC-K:4513-DB HC-KAR Company Limited v. Birendra and Ors.1 and Seema rani and Ors. V. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors.2 are not brought to the notice of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Deepsikha Supra.

entities.text: National Insurance NC: 2025:KHC-K:4513-DB HC-KAR Company Limited v. Birendra and Ors.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Seema rani and Ors. V. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In both cases, Hon'ble Apex Court has considered the fact that even major married earning sons and married daughters are entitled to be counted as dependants of the deceased and to be counted, while making deduction towards personal expenses.
These, two judgments were not brought to the notice in the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Deep Sikha (supra), so the judgment is distinguishable.

On quantum also, he submits that tribunal has properly considered the case and awarded appropriate compensation, which is just and proper and does not call for interference and thus, sought to dismiss the appeal.

5. Having heard counsel appearing for the parties and perusing entire records, points that would arise for consideration are:
"i) Whether Tribunal is justified in fastening the liability primarily on the insurance company to pay (2020) 11 SCC 356 2025 INSC 192 NC: 2025:KHC-K:4513-DB HC-KAR and subsequently to recover the same from the insurer?
ii) Whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal befit in the expression just compensation, if not whether it requires interference?
6. Our answer to the above points for consideration are both in affirmative, for the following :
REASONS 7. Point No.1: The contention of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant-insurance company is that the owner was placed ex-parte and the insurance company has lead evidence and produced document to show that the driver was not holding valid driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
He has also referred to the police record wherein the provisions of Section 180 and 181 of M.V.Act invoked against the owner of the vehicle as well as the driver of the vehicle.
These facts of the case are lost sight by the tribunal while considering the case to order the insurance company primarily to pay the compensation and recover the same from the NC: 2025:KHC-K:4513-DB
Bajaj Allianz
General
Insurance
Co. Ltd vs Sharnamma And Ors on 7 August,

2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20627821/
5 HC-KAR insurer.

The reliance placed on the judgment of Coordinate bench of this Court will not come to the aid of the insurance company for the simple reason that the facts in those cases and the facts on the case on hand as has been rightly contended by the learned counsel appearing for the respondent/ claimant are totally different.

There is clear finding in the judgment referred supra,
that the owner consciously having knowledge of the fact that the driver was not holding appropriate valid licence entrusted him to drive the vehicle.
Herein in the case, the owner was placed ex-parte.
There is no material on record to show that the owner consciously having knowledge of the fact that there is no valid driving license.
Despite entrusted the person to drive the offending vehicle.
In these circumstances, the judgments referred supra will not come to the aid of the appellant-insurance company, distinguishable on fact and are applicable.

Whereas rightly contended by the learned counsel appearing fort the respondent/claimant, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Swaran Singh at para No.110 made it very clear while issuing guidelines, the circumstances where the insurance company is primarily be made liable to pay the compensation and recover the same - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4513-DB HC-KAR from the insurer.
This has been followed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pappu Yadav case.

In lieu of the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court Supra, we hold that there is no infirmity committed by the Tribunal while directing the insurance company primarily liable to pay the compensation and subsequently recover the same from the insurer.
In these circumstances, the findings of the tribunal are justified.
Accordingly, we answer the point No.1 in the affirmative and confirmed the same.
8. Point No.2:

So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant-insurance company would contend that the married daughters are considered while calculating for the loss of dependency counting them while deducting personal expenses and placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Deep Shikha and Anr. Supra.
9.
Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant-insurance company, we have gone through the entire judgment of Deep Shikha.
However, the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Seema rani's and Birendra Singh - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4513-DB HC-KAR supra are not at all cited and discussed in the judgment of Deep Shikha.
In these circumstances, the said judgment is distinguishable and not applicable to the facts of the case on hand.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Seema rani and Birendra Singh, major married and earning son as well as the married daughter are also entitled to be counted as dependent of the deceased.
In view of the same, we hold that the tribunal has rightly come to the conclusion that the married daughters are also entitled to be counted as dependent on the deceased.

Having gone through the entire judgment and award of the concerned tribunal, we find no infirmity in the judgment of the tribunal and accordingly, we affirm the same, answering the points for consideration in affirmative and against the insurance company.

- 12 -  NC: 2025:KHC-K:4513-DB  HC-KAR  ORDER  i) The appeal stands dismissed.
 ii) The amount in deposit be transmitted to the  tribunal for disbursement.
iii) The balance amount along with interest as awarded by the tribunal shall be deposited by the insurance company within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order before the concerned tribunal.

 v) No order as to cost.
